A bullet is fired into a fixed target loses one third of its velocity after travelling \(4 \ cm\). It penetrates further \(D \times 10^{-3} \ m\) before coming to rest. The value of \(D \) is : (assuming constant retardation)

 

[JEE Main 2024, 27 Jan (Shift 2)]

\begin{equation}
\begin{aligned}
&\begin{aligned}
& v^2-u^2=2 a S \\
& \left(\frac{2 u}{3}\right)^2=u^2+2(-a)\left(4 \times 10^{-2}\right) \\
& \Rightarrow \frac{4 u^2}{9}=u^2-2 a\left(4 \times 10^{-2}\right) \\
& \Rightarrow-\frac{5 u^2}{9}=-2 a\left(4 \times 10^{-2}\right) \\
& \Rightarrow 0=\left(\frac{2 u}{3}\right)^2+2(-a)(x) \\
& \Rightarrow-\frac{4 u^2}{9}=-2 a x
\end{aligned}\\
&\text { Dividing equation (1) by (2), we get }\\
&\begin{aligned}
& \frac{5}{4}=\frac{4 \times 10^{-2}}{x} \Rightarrow x=\frac{16}{5} \times 10^{-2} \\
& \Rightarrow x=3.2 \times 10^{-2} \mathrm{~m}=32 \times 10^{-3} \mathrm{~m}
\end{aligned}
\end{aligned}
\end{equation}

questions.question:
The integral \(\int \frac{\left(x^{8}-x^{2}\right) \mathrm{d} x}{\left(x^{12}+3 x^{6}+1\right) \tan ^{-1}\left(x^{3}+\frac{1}{x^{3}}\right)}\) is equal to :

 

[JEE Main 2024, 27 Jan (Shift 2)]
questions.explanation:
Let \(u=\tan^{-1}\left(x^3+\dfrac{1}{x^3}\right)\).

Put \(v=x^3+\dfrac{1}{x^3}\).

Then \(v'=3x^2-\dfrac{3}{x^4}=\dfrac{3(x^6-1)}{x^4}\).

Also, \(1+v^2=1+x^6+2+\dfrac{1}{x^6}=\dfrac{x^{12}+3x^6+1}{x^6}\).

Therefore, \(u'=\dfrac{v'}{1+v^2}=\dfrac{3(x^6-1)}{x^4}\cdot\dfrac{x^6}{x^{12}+3x^6+1}\).

This simplifies to \(u'=\dfrac{3(x^8-x^2)}{x^{12}+3x^6+1}\).

Hence the given integrand is \(\dfrac{1}{3}\dfrac{u'}{u}\).

Therefore, the integral is \(\dfrac{1}{3}\ln|u|+C\).

This can be written as \(\ln\left(|u|^{1/3}\right)+C\).

Substituting \(u=\tan^{-1}\left(x^3+\dfrac{1}{x^3}\right)\), we obtain option A.

\(3x-y+1>0\)

\(x+2y-5<0\)

\(3a^2-a>0\)

Taking the intersection,

\(a\in(-3,0)\cup\left(\dfrac{1}{3},1\right)\)

\(\therefore\) the required set is option \(C\).

questions.question:
If \(\lim _{x \rightarrow 0} \frac{3+\alpha \sin x+\beta \cos x+\log _{e}(1-x)}{3 \tan ^{2} x}=\frac{1}{3}\), then \(2 \alpha-\beta\) is equal to :

 

[JEE Main 2024, 27 Jan (Shift 2)]
questions.explanation:
Near \(x=0\), \(\sin x=x+O(x^3)\), \(\cos x=1-\dfrac{x^2}{2}+O(x^4)\), \(\ln(1-x)=-x-\dfrac{x^2}{2}+O(x^3)\) and \(\tan^2x=x^2+O(x^4)\).

Let the numerator be \(N(x)\).

\(\displaystyle N(x)=3+\alpha x+\beta\left(1-\dfrac{x^2}{2}\right)-x-\dfrac{x^2}{2}+O(x^3)\)

\(\displaystyle \Rightarrow N(x)=(3+\beta)+(\alpha-1)x-\dfrac{\beta+1}{2}x^2+O(x^3)\)

For the limit to be finite, \(3+\beta=0\) and \(\alpha-1=0\).

\(\Rightarrow \beta=-3\) and \(\alpha=1\)

The coefficient of \(x^2\) in the numerator is \(\displaystyle -\dfrac{\beta+1}{2}=1\), while \(3\tan^2x=3x^2+O(x^4)\).

\(\Rightarrow \displaystyle \lim_{x\to0}\dfrac{3+\alpha\sin x+\beta\cos x+\ln(1-x)}{3\tan^2x}=\dfrac13\)

\(\Rightarrow 2\alpha-\beta=2(1)-(-3)=5\)

The correct option is C.

questions.question:
If the area of the region \(\left\{(x, y): 0 \leq y \leq \min \left\{2 x, 6 x-x^{2}\right\}\right\}\) is \(\mathrm{A}\), then \(12 \mathrm{~A}\) is equal to

 

[JEE Main 2024, 27 Jan (Shift 2)]
questions.explanation:
The region satisfies \(0\leq y\leq\min\{2x,6x-x^2\}\).

The line and the parabola intersect when \(2x=6x-x^2\).

Thus \(x^2-4x=0\).

Therefore, \(x=0\) or \(x=4\).

For \(0\leq x\leq4\), we have \(2x\leq6x-x^2\), so the upper boundary is \(y=2x\).

The parabola \(y=6x-x^2\) is non-negative for \(0\leq x\leq6\).

For \(4\leq x\leq6\), the parabola is below the line, so the upper boundary is \(y=6x-x^2\).

Hence \(A=\displaystyle\int_0^4 2x\,dx+\int_4^6(6x-x^2)\,dx\).

The first integral is \(\left[x^2\right]_0^4=16\).

The second integral is \(\left[3x^2-\dfrac{x^3}{3}\right]_4^6\).

At \(x=6\), the value is \(108-72=36\).

At \(x=4\), the value is \(48-\dfrac{64}{3}=\dfrac{80}{3}\).

Therefore, the second integral is \(36-\dfrac{80}{3}=\dfrac{28}{3}\).

Thus \(A=16+\dfrac{28}{3}=\dfrac{76}{3}\).

Hence \(12A=12\cdot\dfrac{76}{3}=304\).

questions.question:
If the sum of squares of all real values of \(\alpha\), for which the lines \(2 x-y+3=0,6 x+3 y+1=0\) and \(\alpha x+2 y-2=0\) do not form a triangle is \(\mathrm{p}\), then the greatest integer less than or equal to \(\mathrm{p}\) is .....

 

[JEE Main 2024, 27 Jan (Shift 2)]
questions.explanation:
The first two lines are \(2x-y+3=0\) and \(6x+3y+1=0\).

Their slopes are \(2\) and \(-2\), so they are neither parallel nor coincident.

The third line is \(\alpha x+2y-2=0\).

The three lines fail to form a triangle if the third line is parallel to either of the first two lines, or if all three lines are concurrent.

The slope of the third line is \(-\dfrac{\alpha}{2}\).

For it to be parallel to \(2x-y+3=0\), we need \(-\dfrac{\alpha}{2}=2\).

Therefore, \(\alpha=-4\).

For it to be parallel to \(6x+3y+1=0\), whose slope is \(-2\), we need \(-\dfrac{\alpha}{2}=-2\).

Therefore, \(\alpha=4\).

Now find the intersection of the first two lines.

From \(2x-y+3=0\), we get \(y=2x+3\).

Substituting in \(6x+3y+1=0\), we get \(6x+3(2x+3)+1=0\).

Thus \(12x+10=0\), so \(x=-\dfrac{5}{6}\).

Then \(y=2\left(-\dfrac{5}{6}\right)+3=\dfrac{4}{3}\).

For concurrence, this point must lie on \(\alpha x+2y-2=0\).

Therefore, \(-\dfrac{5\alpha}{6}+\dfrac{8}{3}-2=0\).

Hence \(-\dfrac{5\alpha}{6}+\dfrac{2}{3}=0\).

Thus \(\alpha=\dfrac{4}{5}\).

The required real values are \(-4\), \(4\), and \(\dfrac{4}{5}\).

The sum of their squares is \(p=16+16+\dfrac{16}{25}=\dfrac{816}{25}\).

Since \(\dfrac{816}{25}=32+\dfrac{16}{25}\), the greatest integer less than or equal to \(p\) is \(32\).

\(\Rightarrow \dfrac{dY}{dX}=\dfrac{X+Y}{X-Y}\)

Integrating, we get

\(\Rightarrow X=1\), \(Y=0\) and \(v=0\)

Comparing with

\(\tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{y-1}{x-1}\right)-\dfrac{1}{\beta}\ln\left(\alpha+\left(\dfrac{y-1}{x-1}\right)^2\right)=\ln|x-1|\)

we get

\(\Rightarrow \alpha=1\)

\(\Rightarrow \beta=2\)

\(\Rightarrow 5\beta+\alpha=10+1=11\)
